# Regular expression pattern from HTTP request data (C#)

`qualor:csharp/regex-injection` · Issue · Severity: Medium · [CWE-1333](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1333.html), [CWE-400](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data in ASP.NET Core (MVC and Web API controllers, Minimal APIs, Razor Pages) that is
used as a regular expression pattern:

- the pattern given to the `Regex` constructor (also `Regex r = new(...)`);
- the pattern argument of the static `Regex.IsMatch`, `Match`, `Matches`, `Replace`, `Split`,
  `Count`, `EnumerateMatches` and `EnumerateSplits`.

Request data used as the input text, or as the replacement string, is not reported, and neither
is a value escaped with `Regex.Escape`, a number, an enum or a pattern picked from a
`static readonly` allow-list. A pattern with a match time-out or `RegexOptions.NonBacktracking` is
still reported: .NET's documentation says these features are no protection against a malicious
pattern.

Request data means the parameters of controller actions, Razor Pages handlers and Minimal API
handlers (strings, string arrays, `StringValues`, forms, uploaded files, the body stream, and any
parameter bound with `[FromQuery]`, `[FromRoute]`, `[FromForm]`, `[FromHeader]`, `[FromBody]` or
`[AsParameters]`), `[BindProperty]` properties, and the request object itself (`Request.Query`,
`Form`, `Headers`, `Cookies`, `RouteValues`, `Body`, ...).
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
The .NET regular expression engine trusts its patterns. A pattern such as `(a+)+$` can take
exponential time to fail on a short input, and other patterns use large amounts of memory to
build; one request can keep a server thread busy for minutes (regular expression denial of
service, ReDoS). A pattern from the request may also match far more than the application meant
to allow.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the search term is used as a pattern.

```csharp
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class SearchController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet]
    public IActionResult Find([FromQuery] string term, [FromQuery] string text)
    {
        return Ok(Regex.IsMatch(text, term));
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the term is escaped and matched literally.

```csharp
using System.Text.RegularExpressions;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class SearchController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet]
    public IActionResult Find([FromQuery] string term, [FromQuery] string text)
    {
        return Ok(Regex.IsMatch(text, Regex.Escape(term)));
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Never build a pattern from request data. To search for the user's text, escape it with
  `Regex.Escape`, or use `string.Contains` and `IndexOf`.
- If users need search syntax, support a small one (wildcards) and translate it into a pattern
  yourself, or let them pick a pattern from an allow-list.
- Time-outs and `RegexOptions.NonBacktracking` limit accidental slowness of your own patterns; they
  do not make a user's pattern safe.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- ASP.NET Core MVC and Web API
- ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs
- ASP.NET Core Razor Pages

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Taint is followed through the methods of one file, not into other files. Request data read
  inside an expression-bodied method (`=> ...`) or a property getter is missed.
- Minimal APIs: a class or record parameter bound from the JSON body without `[FromBody]` is not
  taken for request data, and a handler that is a method of another class is missed. A controller
  named `*Controller` whose base class has another name is missed.
- An enum parameter is reported when the enum is declared after its use or in another file. Only
  allow-lists written as `static readonly` tables of literals count; an equality check or
  `Enumerable.Contains(...)` called as a static method does not, and a variable assigned again
  after a check still counts as checked.
- Only the `Regex` constructor and the static `Regex` methods are checked; a pattern handed to
  another library (a validation attribute, a route constraint) is missed.
- OpenGrep 1.30 does not parse some newer C# syntax (raw strings with `$$"""`, types declared
  without a body such as `class X : Y;`, some multi-line collection expressions); code in those
  parts of a file may be missed.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/csharp/regex/regex-injection.cs`](../../../rules/csharp/regex/regex-injection.cs) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/csharp/regex/regex-injection.yml`](../../../rules/csharp/regex/regex-injection.yml), added in version 2026.10.5.
